title: Visited timing
prompt: In BFS, you should mark a node visited when you OFFER it to the queue, not when you POLL it. Why?
options: Between offer and poll, other nodes could offer it again — the same node enters the queue multiple times
It changes the traversal order to DFS
explanation: Mark-on-poll still terminates but can blow the queue up exponentially in dense graphs. Mark-on-offer guarantees each node is queued once.

title: Drill: build the adjacency list
prompt: From memory: given `n` nodes (0..n-1) and undirected `edges`, return the neighbor count (degree) of each node as an array. Build the adjacency list with computeIfAbsent, then read off sizes. (Yes, you could just count — build the map anyway; that's the drill.)

solution.explanation: Isolated nodes never enter the map — that's why the read side needs getOrDefault. Both lines of the build are pure muscle memory.

hints: Undirected: add the edge in BOTH directions.

title: Drill: count regions (grid DFS)
prompt: From memory (grid flood-fill): count the groups of connected `1`s in `grid` (4-directional). Scan every cell; each unvisited 1 starts a region you sink with DFS.
hints: Each scan-found 1 is a new region; DFS sinks the whole region to 0 so it isn't recounted.
